title: Jeremy Corbell and the missing page of the Shellenberger-released government document

tellings.quote: Jeremy Corbel went on that whole tangent about the the missing page and the fact that he >> his name was taken off of the whole thing and it just really rubbed me the wrong way.

plain: A government report on UFO data, made public in 2024, is said to have lost a page, and with it the name of Jeremy Corbell, a figure in UFO circles. The hip hop artist Flying Lotus tells Michels that Corbell "went on that whole tangent about the missing page" and his name being "taken off," and says it "rubbed me the wrong way." The document is the so-called Immaculate Constellation report, which is unsigned and of disputed origin. The journalist Michael Shellenberger delivered it to Congress, and Rep. Nancy Mace entered it into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024. A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown later said he wrote it, and a Pentagon spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report calls itself a "public version of the author's report," cleared for release by the State Department. Mace told the hearing it ran to 12 pages, but the copy on her House site has 11 unnumbered pages. Neither that copy nor the hearing record says what the fuller version contained, so the claim that a missing page carried Corbell's name rests on the tellers' word.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report calls itself a "public version of the author's report", reviewed and approved for release by the State Department, and the copy on Rep. Nancy Mace's House site has 11 unnumbered pages where Mace told the hearing it had 12. Neither the copy nor the hearing record says what the fuller version held, so a missing page bearing Jeremy Corbell's name rests on the tellers' account.
